notes: Behaviour: with BLOCK CONTAINS 3 RECORDS and no PADDING CHARACTER clause, two 5-character records make a 10-byte file (ALPHADELTA) and the third READ is at end (status 10); nothing pads. The refuter's only doubt was that docs/CONFORMANCE.md had no determination. The pinned tree now has one: §3.6, row 'The PADDING CHARACTER clause (85, 2002; deleted from 2014)' (kb/Work PB5069, PB5070), 'a null facility in function ... no padding character is written or bypassed', resting on GR2. Under GR2 no padding occurs on any file this implementation supports, so the GR5 default is never used, and the implementor has stated so.

next.reason: 1985 PADDING CHARACTER clause GR5: 'If the PADDING CHARACTER clause is not specified, the value used for the padding character will be defined by the implementor.' 2023 has no PADDING CHARACTER clause (absent from the file control formats of §2023:12.4.5.1 (General formats)) and no implementor-defined item in §2023:A.1 for a padding character value; §2023:9.1.1 'Padding characters are added or deleted as necessary' sets no default value. No 2023 rule carries this rule.
